Overall: 4/10

Pacify is a game that attempts to deliver a tense co-op horror experience but ultimately falls short due to its lackluster design and repetitive gameplay. The game has up to four co-op players, including you, working together to complete tasks while avoiding a relentless AI-controlled enemy, but this core mechanic quickly becomes more frustrating than frightening. To put it bluntly, none of the levels manage to offer an engaging or fun experience. Each environment feels uninspired, with objectives that grow tedious after just a few attempts on ANY of the missions.
The atmosphere, while initially eerie, loses its impact as the jump scares and enemy behavior become predictable and honestly just monotonous. The game’s simplistic design leaves little room for strategy, reducing the co-op experience to frantic running and random item collection. Furthermore, the AI enemy usually feels more unfair than challenging, often resulting in irritating and unsatisfying encounters.
Even at its low $5 price point, Pacify fails to justify its cost due to a complete and utter lack of meaningful content or compelling gameplay. Additionally, there are much better indie horror titles with MUCH better content around the same price point. This game may be fun to laugh at with your friends for half an hour, but for genuine horror fans seeking a deeper, more rewarding experience, this one is very hard to recommend...

Dolls everywhere you look.

Pacify currently offers a choice of three maps. Of course, a different map, a different story and a different killer. In the case of the first variant (Mansion), our adventure begins in front of a large manor house and the night and a heavy downpour with a storm work on the atmosphere. Upon entering the house, the player is not predictably surprised that many doors require a key. The search, collection and pursuit cycle therefore begins. The most important items to collect are dolls. Pacify offers exactly two versions - the "good" and the "bad" ones. There is no confusion, the bad dolls look as if Mattel has decided to do a special limited edition dedicated to black metal. In addition, these creatures giggle mischievously and try to run away from you. Your task is to find all the bad toys and burn them in the basement. Why? In them is the power of the hunting killer. On this map, a tragically deceased girl is guarding her territory, and her death is recorded in pieces on pieces of paper throughout the house. With each evil doll burned, the killer becomes more dangerous, faster, and how many times he seems to have learned to teleport.
Other maps have their own stories, but the principle is always the same.

Pacify qualitatively corresponds to the price at which you buy it. The time investment will also not be the biggest - this one-off with a minimal drum feeling will entertain demanding horror players barely for the evening. [b] 20% [/b]

This is one of the best horror games I've played.  I can only play it for short time periods because the adrenaline rush makes me nauseous.  The pitter-patter sound of that ghost girl walking around just terrifies me.  As such, sadly, this is a game I'll never even come close to finishing.

You can play this single, co-op, or PVP.  You're a paranormal investigator (a.k.a. ghost hunter), and you enter the basement of an old funeral home.  It's 3 stories, plus the basement, so it's easy to get temporarily lost.  Starting out, it's pretty simple.  You have to get a key to the second floor, then a key to the attic, and then release the special marked dolls in the attic which seem to be alive.  It's creepy how they giggle and run around, and I believe there are 9 of them.

Once the marked dolls are released, things get harder.  You now have to catch all the marked dolls, one by one, take them to the basement, and burn them in the furnace.  There are also regular dolls (which don't move) laying around the house.  The ghost girl pitter-patters around the house, and every now and then she gets demonized and comes after you.  Grab a regular doll and give it to her, and she'll calm down and go back to just being ghost girl for a little while.

But beware, because the more marked dolls you burn, the quicker she gets demonized again, giving you less and less time to burn all of the remaining marked dolls.  And if she catches you without one of the regular dolls in your hand, it's game over because she turns you into a doll.  There are also 2 other scenarios which have been added to the game over time.  For one of them, you're on a farm running from a farmer.  He's either a fast-running zombie, or a crazed cannibal.  For the last scenario, you're in the woods.  I haven't played this one yet, so I don't know what the monster is here.

Controls are easy.  There's walk, run, jump, flashlight on/off, and item grab/drop.  Graphics are awesome.  Some of the achievements are for single, some are for co-op, and some are for PVP.  Sometimes it's hard to find a multiplayer game to join, and you can't play in multiplayer by yourself, so you should try to talk a friend into buying the game.  Also, if you get turned into a doll in co-op, one of the other players can save you.  They throw you in the furnace and you return to human size again.

Pacify is a horror game, where you go into a house to check what happened, because the girl who lives there, she is possesed or something like that, and you have to break this curse.

I played this game in coop mode with another person, so this review will be based on that.

The graphics is... weird. I mean some things looks good, most of the props, items in the house looks good, but the outside part or the wall's texture in the cellar for example is just horrible. If you play in multiplayer and the other player using it's flashlight, for you that light is just weak... but in game the flashlight is strong, but only for that player who using the light. So graphics is weird, not the best in 2019, but you can live with it.

Controls working just fine. You don't need lot of buttons for this one, just direction keys, crouch / jump and action key. That's all.

Sound and music is another story. You can determine the source of sounds in this game sometimes, but when it's about floor difference, than sometimes you can't tell that, if it's next to you or above to you. There are just a few music in the game, in the menu and maybe the outro scences has music, but that's all. Not a bad thing, but not really memorable.

So... about the gameplay. I don't want to say this as a bad thing, but the gameplay is really similar to the first Slender Man game, where you had to collect pages to stop the monster. This is really similar to it. You need to collect 9 evil doll and burn them in the cellar's furnace, meanwhile if you burn a doll, the girl become more aggressive. You need wood and matches to lit the furnace, and also you need different keys for different rooms to open doors in the house, so you can't really just camp at one place. Another factor, is the dolls can move around, so you definetly need to look around for them. You can read articles and diaries to find out more about this curse too. If the girl gets you when she is possesed or something, you become her doll. You get smaller, you can't lit the furnace and collect dolls, you just kinda spectating the situation. However if the other player lit the furnace, you can turn back to human there. Your only protection against her, if you find a normal doll. If you give it to her, she start to play with that for a short time, and she starts to attack you again.

The game has potential, nice ideas but it's time to talk about the problems. First one, is that the game is not really good for Single player. You can play it, and it's really difficult, but you can see that the game is definetly made for more than one player, so you need company for this one.
The dolls and keys location is random everytime you start to play, but if you find that 6-7 places in the house where the  game spawn these most of the time, you won't have a problem, however the wood locations are not fixed.
You can "cheat" this game, if you know it flows, and I can't belive that the dev(s) didn't fixed that bug, which can break the whole game and win it in speedrun time.
Sadly, [spoiler]if you know, what to expect in the game (jumpscare scenes), then the game won't be that scary anymore.
Another problem, is the ending. Basically, you fight for your life and then when you finally break the curse, you just get the girl and start to experiment her... and this scene felt like I wasted my time, I wanted something more for the ending.[/spoiler]
I have to mention, is the game is not long. Even tho, the game has a PvP mode, which is the same collecting gameplay which you had before, but it's for points now, you can play through it in 2 hours if you quickly find out, what is going on.

So there are problems with this game, but I have to tell you... for a first experince this game can work out really well. It's scary for the first time, thrilling and interesting at the same time, and if you got friends to play with this is actually more fun to do. I can recommend to play it for one time only, because replaying this is not that fun.

What a fun game! I played both the Dolls and Farm level with my buddy and we had a blast, we jumped a few times.
The sounds were perfectly done, it leaves you feeling anxious the whole time.

The new farm level was my favorite, it felt like a puzzle, thinking was involved in the farm level unlike the dolls level which felt like an egg hunt.
The game is pretty short, it took my friend and I around 3.5 hours to beat both levels, hopefully they’ll add more levels in the future.
 
If you buy this game pick it up with a friend or two, you’ll enjoy it so much more!
